claims.text: Funding is available for conference support.
There are three streams of conference support.
Stream A offers up to £200 for travel and accommodation for Genetics Society or Special Interest Group meetings.
Stream B offers up to £500 for non-Society genetics conferences.
Stream B offers up to £750 for two Adelphi Genetics Forum co-sponsored awards a year for PhD students only.
Stream C offers up to £300 for registration for virtual conferences.
The funding is for Genetics Society junior scientist members.
The conferences must be on research in Genetics.

claims.text: Grants are available to support attendance of Genetics Society junior scientist members at conferences on research in Genetics.
Scheme (A) is open to undergraduate, Master’s and PhD student members and postdoctoral scientist members within six years of their PhD viva.
Scientists who obtained their PhD more than six years ago are not eligible for Scheme (A).
Schemes (B) & (C) are open to PhD student and postdoctoral scientist members within six years of their PhD viva.
Undergraduate or Master’s students are not eligible for Schemes (B) & (C).
Scientists who obtained their PhD more than six years ago are not eligible for Schemes (B) & (C).
Schemes (B) & (C) are open to members with a UK base wishing to attend conferences outside of the UK.
Schemes (B) & (C) are open to non-UK-based members wishing to attend a conference in the UK.
Applications from bases outside the UK for conference attendance outside the UK cannot be considered.
A maximum of one grant per two years will be awarded for applications to Scheme (B) or (C).
Applicants must present a poster or give a talk at the conference.
Supervisors providing support letters must be current members of the Genetics Society and include their membership number.
Grant recipients will be asked to write a short report that may be published in the Genetics Society Newsletter.
Grants up to £200 are available for travel and accommodation for Scheme (A) meetings.
There is no limit to the frequency that Scheme (A) grants can be applied for.
Grants of up to £500 are available for Scheme (B) conferences.
Up to two Scheme (B) Conference grants per year will be co-sponsored by the Adelphi Genetics Forum, providing up to £750.
The Adelphi Genetics Forum co-sponsored award is only open to registered PhD student members who will take up the award before their PhD graduation date.
If unsuccessful for the Adelphi Genetics Forum co-sponsored award, applications will be automatically considered for a standard stream B grant.
Grants of up to £300 are available to cover registration costs for virtual conferences (Scheme C).
The virtual conference grant is available to UK-based members for genetics-related virtual conferences anywhere.
The virtual conference grant is available to non-UK-based members for UK-based Genetics related virtual conferences.
Applications should be submitted by bi-monthly deadlines: 1st day of February, April, June, August, October and December.
Applications should be made by logging into the mySociety membership portal.
The conference must take place AFTER the application deadline.
For Genetics Society and Special Interest Group (SIG) meetings, applications should be submitted online before the registration deadline of the meeting.
Queries regarding the application process can be directed to theteam@genetics.org.uk.

claims.text: Grants are available to support undergraduate students.
The grants are for students gaining experience in genetics through a research project.
The research project takes place during the summer holiday.
The deadline for 2026 applications is March 31st, 2026.
The project should be achievable within an eight-week timeframe.
Students must be able to attend a UK-based Summer School workshop at the end of the research period.
The Summer School workshop is taking place at the University of Oxford.
The Summer School workshop is from September 2nd to 4th.
Applicants must find a research area of genetics and match it to a research group leader.
The student and the group leader must be members of the Genetics Society.
Applications are made by the student in partnership with the group leader.
The Genetics Society welcomes applications from all sections of the community.
The summer studentship grant includes a £425/week allowance for up to 8 weeks.
The grant includes up to £750 to cover host laboratory expenses.
A Carer’s Award is available to cover childcare or other responsibility costs.
Only travel within the UK can be funded.
Summer studentships cannot be used to part-fund a larger project.
Extension of honours projects or early starts for PhD students are not eligible.
Only one application per student and lab group may be submitted.
Applications must include a project outline, a project plan, and a personal statement.
Successful applicants will be asked to write a short report within two months of project completion.
The summer studentship is open to all undergraduate students except those in their first or final year.
The project must be based at a UK university.
Funding is not provided for travel to the UK from overseas.
The purpose of the studentship is to provide hands-on experience in a research environment.
The studentship includes a place at the Genetics Society Summer Studentship Workshop in the UK.
Travel to the workshop from within the UK and the cost of accommodation and meals are included.
The group leader will help write the project in an area they work on.
Membership of the Genetics Society costs £10 for undergraduate students.
The grant cannot be used to support an extended honours project.
The grant cannot be used for an early start to postgraduate studies.
If a student has received funding from another source, they cannot apply for this studentship.
The success rate was around 25% last year (2024).
To host a Summer Studentship, the research group leader must be a member of The Genetics Society.
The student hosted must be an undergraduate based at any university.
The student can be of any nationality.
Applications from outside the UK are eligible.
The Society can arrange upfront student support payments in exceptional circumstances if the institution cannot.
The group leader must help the student complete certain sections of the application form.
